claims.statement: Strap uses Postgres 17 locally (postgres:17.6-alpine loopback-bound on 127.0.0.1:55433) and 18 on Railway, accessed via the Drizzle ORM, with no database REST endpoint or RLS. Hosted connections require verified TLS and a transaction pooler; the driver uses one connection and disables prepared statements.

Better Auth (lib/auth/create-auth.ts) enables email/password with required email verification and session-revoking password resets, upgrades imported legacy bcrypt hashes on first successful sign-in via an after-hook guarded by optimistic concurrency, supports Google + X social providers with trusted linking for Google only, and uses a 60-second session cookie cache with database-backed rate limiting (100/60s).

Authorization is enforced in application code via lib/authz/policies.ts row scopes (the equivalents of retired RLS policies), not the database: queries are gated by actor kind, ownership, and Company role, with the service context bypassing scopes for admin reads after an app-level role check.

Migrations are ordered SQL files in db/migrations/ with 0000_baseline.sql as the single squashed baseline; Drizzle generates forward migrations, but function edits require a hand-written SQL migration plus a reference-file update. Creed- and Stripe-named schema objects are not renamed during the Strap rebrand.

AI credential resolution (lib/ai/credits.ts) has two modes: Included ('credits') uses OPENROUTER_PLATFORM_KEY with no credits sold/debited, and BYOK ('byok') decrypts a valid Personal/Company key. Absent platform key requires BYOK. Both modes select the model server-side per feature with no in-app picker.

lib/ai/credits.ts enforces operational limits (not billing): a process-local 20-req/60s burst limit per user, and a trailing-24h at-cost ceiling defaulting to $0.50/user (overridable via INCLUDED_AI_DAILY_LIMIT_USD) by summing estimated_cost_usd from creed_ai_usage for the user's credits-mode rows. There is no debit RPC, prepaid balance, checkout, or runtime payment.

Every AI call is recorded into creed_ai_usage (recordAiUsage) with at-cost estimated_cost_usd, charged_micro_usd, token counts, model id/quality, feature, and Strap id (company usage stamped with the Company Strap id; personal left null) for visibility and quota, not billing.

Model selection (lib/ai/model-catalog.ts) is server-side per feature: Analysis defaults to anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, Tab/Panel to openai/gpt-oss-120b (throughput-routed), BYOK defaults stay on first-party OpenAI models; env overrides are ANALYSIS_MODEL/TAB_MODEL/PANEL_MODEL and BYOK_* variants. Agent model override is STRAP_AGENT_MODEL (fallback CREED_AGENT_MODEL); BYOK agent defaults to openai/gpt-5.

lib/ai/openrouter.ts (callOpenRouter + streamOpenRouter) requests usage.include=true to get OpenRouter's authoritative billed cost (falling back to catalog estimate), pins BYOK openai/* models to the native OpenAI route via lib/ai/openrouter-routing.ts, and translates 401/402/429 into mode-specific user-facing errors; HTTP-Referer is derived from the deployed origin.

A single GitHub OAuth App backs both Personal and Company version-control connections (repo sync, not sign-in). /api/app/github/authorize mints a nonce cookie carrying mode+creedId; /auth/github/callback verifies the single-use cookie, re-checks the session and company role, exchanges the code, fetches the GitHub viewer, and stores the encrypted token (personal -> creed_integrations, company -> creed_company_github_integration, owner/admin only).

GitHub token refresh is proactive (~2 min before expiry) and retries once on a bad-credentials/expired/401 error, for both personal (withAuthenticatedGitHubAccess) and company (withCompanyGitHubAccess) flows; a malformed/undecryptable company token degrades to a reconnect prompt rather than throwing.

New Personal/Company GitHub configs default to strap.md (the schema path column defaults to 'strap.md'). lib/profile-file.ts tries strap.md then legacy creed.md for a blank/strap.md path, treats any other stored path as exact, and push refuses (409) to create a competing strap.md when a read resolved legacy creed.md.

GitHub push (POST /api/app/github/push) fetches the remote SHA/content-hash, refuses on a legacy-path conflict, and PUTs via GitHub Contents optimistic concurrency (default message 'Update Strap'). Company managers push to the Company target on the team token; personal Straps push on the user's connection. Sync bookkeeping is written after success.

Personal pull has preview/apply phases: apply replaces active sections, clears proposals, retains archived sections not reintroduced, and forces imported sections to agentWritable/agentPermission=propose. Company pull is not implemented (both preview and apply throw). Preview/apply is not bound to a freshly fetched remote SHA, so stale preview data can be applied.

lib/strap-markdown.ts + lib/rich-text.ts round-trip formatting: push shifts section headings down one level, pull un-shifts them, and the accent color survives via an HTML comment (<!-- creed:accent=... -->) that is read back and stripped. Legacy section names map to canonical ids. lib/creed-markdown.ts is a deprecated re-export shim.

Transactional email (verification, password resets, Company invites) is sent via Resend's HTTP API in lib/email.ts with no SDK; it fails closed (returns ok:false and logs) and never throws, so an invite row is still created and resendable when RESEND_API_KEY/RESEND_FROM_EMAIL are unset. Tests capture links in memory; password resets revoke sessions.

lib/marketing/pricing.ts PLAN_FACTS is the canonical pricing source shared by cards, crawlable reference, schema, and /llms.txt: Open ($0, self-host, BYOK), Personal ($0, hosted, included or BYOK), Company ($0, hosted, included or Company BYOK, unlimited members). Stripe is removed from dependencies, .env.example, and runtime routes.

Company creation is direct/idempotent via POST /api/app/company (provisionCompany, one owned company per user; retries return the existing shell); invites are not purchased seats. Historical creed_entitlements, creed_company_billing, Stripe columns, and seat-purchase records remain as forward-only history and do not describe live billing.

lib/legacy-subscriptions.ts + lib/legacy-subscription-deletion.ts support owner-only legacy offboarding: they read and schedule cancel_at_period_end on pre-existing subscriptions (requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) and block account/Company deletion until every legacy subscription is ended or scheduled-to-cancel. The key should be removed only after all legacy subscriptions are canceled.

scripts/migrate-from-supabase.mts is a one-time cutover tool reading STRAP_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL: default prints counts, --apply requires an empty target, imports in one transaction reconciling all 37 tables, resetting identity sequences, preserving IDs/hashes/ciphertext, re-encrypting Vault plaintext in memory, with no force flag and no session migration.

STRAP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET wins over CREED_ENCRYPTION_SECRET for token/payload encryption, STRAP_AGENT_MODEL over CREED_AGENT_MODEL for the agent model, STRAP_CSP_ENFORCE over CREED_CSP_ENFORCE for CSP enforcement, and STRAP_DIST_DIR over CREED_DIST_DIR for dev build dir. These are separate from BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, STRAP_VAULT_SECRET, and STRAP_MAINTENANCE_SECRET.

next.config.ts constrains known origins (CSP connect-src allows self + openrouter + github; frame-ancestors self), ships CSP as Report-Only by default (STRAP_CSP_ENFORCE switches to enforcing), pins user-dependent routes to private/no-store, long-caches /assets/*, and dev builds to .next-runtime. Root tsconfig.json excludes both CLI packages.

POST /api/internal/maintenance requires Authorization: Bearer STRAP_MAINTENANCE_SECRET and prunes activity older than 90 days and expired device/authorization codes, returning/logging counts only; the daily GitHub Actions workflow needs STRAP_SITE_URL and STRAP_MAINTENANCE_SECRET.
